findings.issue: Task 6's frontmatter declares depends_on: [1] only, but Task 6's own Dependencies/Details sections state the golden-file regeneration must happen on code where Task 5's dom_blocks migration is ALREADY merged: 'Пересъёмку делай на коде, где Task 5 уже влит, иначе рискуешь смешать в одном diff'е два изменения — и условие «меньше картинок и ничего больше» станет непроверяемым.' Task 5 and Task 6 are both Wave 2 tasks with no edge between them, and grouping into a wave is precisely the signal an orchestrator uses to parallelize independent tasks. If Task 6 runs before or concurrently with Task 5, it regenerates tests/fixtures/orangetrack_golden.json (and edits tests/test_orangetrack_golden.py to thread the image-limit parameter) against pre-refactor code. The clean, single-purpose golden diff is the sole artifact backing the operator's two-condition approval of the AC9/AC10 deviation (tech-spec User-Spec Deviations, approved 2026-08-03) — if that diff mixes Task 5's refactor with Task 6's cap, the approval condition is silently violated and nobody would know, since Task 6's own decisions.md diff entry would already have been written against the wrong baseline.
findings.fix: Add 5 to Task 6's depends_on (i.e. depends_on: [1, 5]) so the orchestrator sequences Task 5 before Task 6 instead of relying on a prose note inside Task 6's Details section that a parallel-wave executor is unlikely to read as a hard gate.
